namedLocations.description: A ZIP Code is a postal code used by the United States Postal Service (USPS) in a system it introduced in 1963. The term ZIP is an acronym for Zone Improvement Plan; it was chosen to suggest that the mail travels more efficiently and quickly (zipping along) when senders use the code in the postal address. The basic format consists of five digits. An extended ZIP+4 code was introduced in 1983 which includes the five digits of the ZIP Code, followed by a hyphen and four additional digits that reference a more specific location.

transcript.text: Hello and welcome to the On Print Shop customer management tutorial series.
In today's business landscape, managing your customers efficiently and building strong relationships is more important than ever.
In this video, we'll talk about how you can manage your customers in the On Print Shop today.
We will walk you through the customer registration process, how these customer details are displayed in the admin panel, and how we can add or manage these details.
So for the registration flow, let's go to the storefront.
When any new customer lands on your homepage and chooses to register, they will click on this login register link from the header and one pop up will appear for the same.
For the registration, they can either manually sign up using the register link or register and login using their social media accounts.
These options are based on the configuration you may have performed in the admin panel.
So when the customer clicks on the register link, they will be redirected to the sign up page.
Here the sign up or registration form can be of two types, a detailed or Quick 1 based on the setting.
For this we have a setting in the Site settings section Enable Quick Registrations.
You can choose to enable and display the quick registration form for default store customers, all public and private store customers or to both.
With the None option, you can disable this quick form and the detailed form will appear on the sign up page.
Let's assume that the customers have registered, so from where can you check their details?
The answer is from the website customers section of the admin panel.
On this page you will see all your website customers with their details such as name, e-mail ID, store type.

Like if they have registered from the default store or any of your public private stores, contact details, customer level settings on which date they registered, account status and action drop down for you to take some actions.
In the store type, you can see that this customer has been assigned to the Platinum user group.
And in the settings column, you can see that the customer has some pay on account limit for order placement and he has been exempted from tax also.
So let's check how these fields and settings are managed.
Let's select this first customer, click on the actions drop down and then select Edit.
On the edit customer screen you can manage all the details such as their user type, name, e-mail ID, etcetera.
Now we have this user group setting.
The advantage of creating a group is that if you want to give special discounts or share coupons to some specific group of users, then you can create a group and assign those customers to the group.
This also can be used to separate your family, friends or zone wise users.
Let's add this customer to a group.
Either you can select from the existing groups or you can create one group using the plus icon.
Click on the plus icon, then click on the Add button.
Enter the name of the group and then save from the drop down.
You can now select the newly created group to assign this customer to this group.
If any sales agent has added this customer, then you can associate the sales agent's name with the customer from the Select Sales Agent field.
Now, sometimes it may happen that the customer has forgotten their password and asked you to reset that.
So for such scenarios, you can select the Set to option in the password field, generate a password and then share it with them to restore their account.
Moving below we have the customer settings section.
This section is to manage the status of the customer account, enable the notifications for the customer, exempt the customer from tax and even manage the language and currency.

If you want to offer the customer some time to make their payments, then you can enter the days in the payment due days such as 30 days and the customer will be able to make the payment within 30 days of invoice generation.
Regarding payment methods, you can enable the pay on account payment method and give a pay on limit to be used while placing the order.
Please note that this setting will only appear when the Pay on account payment is enabled on the payment methods page.
Next we have the partial payment method similar to Pay on Account.
You can allow this method customer wise by enabling the setting and then assigning any payment term to the customer.

These terms are created in the Payment Term master screen so when allowed the customer can use this method to place the order and their entire total amount will be converted into configured installments.
For more information on Partial payment you can refer to our help portal.
You can also choose to enable or disable the selected Customers Reward module.
Lastly, you also have the option to manage their addresses using the Manage Address section.
Click on the Manage Address button from the top right corner and on the next page you will see the shipping and billing addresses added by the customer.
You have the option to edit the existing addresses, or you can even add a new address from your end too if the customer has shared their details.
Once you're done with managing the customer account details, save all the changes on the listing page.
You can now see that the user group of the customer is there along with the sales agent's name, pay on limit, etc.
So this is how you can manage the registration and customer details from the admin panel.
If you have any questions, our support executives are here to help.
Just reach out through live chat on on printshop.com.
Thanks for tuning in.
